scope: Proposition 4.5 (Compatible product presentations) of the manuscript “Projective-space bases of Lagrangian fibrations” (preprints/Projective-Space-Bases-of-Lagrangian-Fibrations-September-23-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 041 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5fdf543649f1469a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The following data exist along S0. 1. There are finitely many normal finite Galois quasi-étale charts Vα → Bα, with deck groups Γα and with Bα → B separated and étale, covering S0. They are maximal at every point over S0. 2. Normalized main overlaps give an étale groupoid along the reduced inverse images Sα ⊂ Vα. Its quotient is the stack S of Proposition 4.3. Writing I for the marked ideal on the object charts, the same finite diagrams define, for every k ≥ 1, a proper separated Deligne– Mumford stack Sk, with S1 = S. Its coarse space is finite over B and projective. 3. A finite family of étale refinements of the object charts covers their closed strata and has the marked-product presentations of Lemma 4.4. All transition maps come from the normalized ambient overlaps and preserve I exactly. Their restrictions are consequently compatible for all powers Ik. 4. The normalized source charts give ordinary pullback and descent of coherent sheaves on any Sk to coherent sheaves on X supported over S0. These assertions are encoded by finitely many algebraic schemes, morphisms, ideals and identities. In particular they can be spread simultaneously before choosing any order of Frobenius pullback.
